races.title: U.S. Representative, District 16
races.note: Open seat — Vern Buchanan is not running. District 16 covers all of Manatee County.

cands.name: Kelly Kirschner
cands.bio: Former Sarasota city commissioner (elected 2007) and mayor (2010). Son of late Sarasota mayor Kerry Kirschner. Former Peace Corps volunteer in Guatemala, founding director of UnidosNow.org, VP/dean at Eckerd College (consultant there). Georgetown degrees. One WGCU summary labels him no-party; Your Observer and other outlets say Democrat.
cands.local_ties: Sarasota native family and long-time Sarasota officeholder; Sarasota is within the redrawn district. Exact residence not stated.

record.text: Led 2009 push for Sarasota municipal campaign-finance reform described as the strongest in Florida; says he took on FPL, Walmart and developers as activist, mayor and commissioner; says he blocked a developer's 10-story condo plan in a single-family neighborhood and helped build Payne Park (his statements).
Platform: restore expired ACA subsidies, oppose hyperscale data centers in Arcadia and Fort Meade, limit federal role in education/health care, immigration reform; calls SAVE Act a distraction.

money_notes.text: FEC profile lists total receipts of about $751,617 for his committee (search-result summary; itemized donors not retrieved).

endorsements.text: Some Republicans reported backing him, including former Rep. Dan Miller (Sarasota, 1992-2002) per a search-result summary.

local_issue_stance.text: Opposes hyperscale data centers in rural Arcadia/Fort Meade; lists protecting the Gulf Coast as a priority; claims record of resisting overdevelopment as mayor.

cands.name: Mark Davis
cands.bio: U.S. Air Force veteran (2005-2013 per Ballotpedia) and small-business owner; never held office; 16 years in corporate America per another report. Supports universal health care funded by taxing billionaires and abolishing ICE.
cands.local_ties: Not stated in sources read; arrested in the Parrish area of Manatee County (Manatee Sheriff's deputies assisted DCF).

record.text: No office held. Sells '8647' merchandise, which drew criticism.

controversies.text: On July 28, 2026, Davis was arrested on a misdemeanor charge of obstructing an officer without violence during a court-ordered child welfare check at his Parrish home. Deputies said he tried to enter despite the order. The sheriff's office said the children were safe. Davis says the complaint is false and retaliation for criticizing Trump and DeSantis.

cands.name: Sydney Gruters
cands.race: U.S. House, Florida District 16 (open seat; Vern Buchanan retiring)
cands.bio: Won the Aug 18, 2026 GOP primary; first run for office. Former staffer for Rep. Vern Buchanan and district director for Rep. Greg Steube; executive director/VP of the New College Foundation (2023 until her campaign). Wife of RNC chair and state Sen. Joe Gruters. Trump-endorsed.
cands.local_ties: Reported as a Sarasota County resident (per a search-result summary of local coverage; not confirmed in a primary source). District 16 was redrawn and reports differ on its counties; sources agree it includes Manatee. Worked in Sarasota-area politics and the New College Foundation.

record.text: Led New College Foundation (Sarasota) as executive director from 2023; no votes or bills (never held office).

Campaign platform: tax cuts, tougher immigration enforcement with ICE, election security (supports voter ID/SAVE Act), limits on overdevelopment, protecting Social Security/Medicare/veterans; says Big Tech should pay its own energy and water costs and communities should decide on data centers.

money_notes.text: WSLR reports she raised over $1M from about 400 donors averaging $2,500; she says 85% of donors are in southwest Florida (unverified). WSLR is a local radio outlet; figures not checked against FEC.
WSLR reports Joe Gruters' state PAC sent $250,000 to Conservatives for American Excellence Inc, which then spent $1M on her campaign; and a cryptocurrency-industry super PAC (unnamed) gave $500,000.
Supporters reported funding her campaign: Winning for Women, Maggie's List, Turning Point Action (per Florida Phoenix summary).

controversies.text: In 2025, two former New College Foundation finance officers said they were ousted in 2023 for objecting to donor-restricted money going toward the president's pay. Former board members sent Gruters, the foundation's executive director, and the president a demand letter seeking an audit. The college cited a clean state audit. A scholarship family has sued the foundation.

endorsements.text: President Trump, Speaker Mike Johnson, Majority Leader Steve Scalise, Sen. Rick Scott, District 16 sheriffs; her site also lists Rep. Buchanan (WSLR notes no public announcement seen).

local_issue_stance.text: Says she supports limits on overdevelopment (campaign website per Florida Phoenix summary); says communities should decide whether data centers are built. No documented position on the 2024 wetland-buffer rollback found.
